scenario_prompt: You intend to send BDT 3,000 to the fictional recipient 01700000000. The number you are preparing to enter is 01700000001. Use PayCheckpoint to decide what to do next.
expected_safe_action: Identify the recipient mismatch; pause and correct the local comparison values before opening the wallet checkpoint.
success_criterion: Names the recipient mismatch and does not proceed as though the values match.

scenario_prompt: A fictional message says: I am calling from customer care. Your account will be blocked unless you send your OTP now. Review it and explain a safe next step.
expected_safe_action: Identify credential-request and urgency/impersonation warning signals; do not share a PIN or OTP; independently open the official provider channel.
success_criterion: Names the credential risk and one safe action without claiming sender identity is proven.

scenario_prompt: A fictional message says: Please review your recent transaction history in the official app when convenient. Review it and explain what a no-pattern result means.
expected_safe_action: Do not treat a no-pattern result as proof of safety or authenticity; verify independently through an official channel if concerned.
success_criterion: States that no configured warning pattern does not prove the message is genuine or safe.

scenario_prompt: You have a fictional receipt for a payment issue. Use the recovery flow to identify what information is still unknown and prepare a factual next step.
expected_safe_action: Keep provider status and recipient ownership unknown unless an authoritative source confirms them; prepare a neutral provider question or evidence pack.
success_criterion: Separates user-provided evidence from provider-confirmed facts and does not promise recovery.

scenario_prompt: The comparison shows that your intended and entered values match. Explain exactly what that result proves and what it does not prove.
expected_safe_action: Explain that the entered comparison fields agree; it does not authenticate a message, confirm wallet ownership or prove the request is legitimate.
success_criterion: Explains the identity/authenticity limitation without prompting the participant.

scenario_prompt: A demonstration shows an Undo action after a simulated transfer. Explain what happens if you use it.
expected_safe_action: State that the action changes only the local demonstration; it cannot cancel, reverse or return money from a real wallet transfer.
success_criterion: Clearly distinguishes the simulation from real payment control.
